text: Time series intelligence meets real-time context. I B M Granite Time Series models now run live inside Confluent, pretrained to scale across plants, stores, SKUs and customers, efficient on standard CPUs, and learning as each event lands.
Take one store on a hot day. The forecast reads the heat wave and sees the stockout coming, so the empty shelf is flagged in seconds,
and the next order is optimized to keep it full, while the decision still matters.

That works because the intelligence lives where the data already flows. Confluent streams and governs every event, and Granite turns it into a decision in under a second, while the usual way is still a day behind.
So your teams ship a forecast in one step instead of six, get thirty-two percent less error than a seasonal baseline, and stop waiting on nightly scoring runs.

Time series models optimize mission-critical decisions as each event lands. On a chocolate line, temper is forecast on every reading, so setpoints adjust before a new cocoa butter lot turns into rework.
Across thousands of signals, each series gets its own expected band, so weekend peaks pass and only the real breaks are flagged.
In retail, one model forecasts every SKU in every store and reorders at the service level you choose.
In payments, each card is scored against its own normal before authorization, so card testing is held and travelers get through.
Years of history become searchable by shape, so one sketch finds every signal that looked like this.
On the trading desk, a volume forecast with a probability band paces large orders to the market.

And it already works in the field. Telco tickets open only on confirmed causes, two models replaced thirty in a cement plant and lifted accuracy to ninety-nine percent, and trading forecasts carry about ten percent less error.
